catalog_identity.rule: Every read is pinned to one immutable finite catalog revision and returns that identity.
catalog_identity.replacement_rule: A catalog replacement creates a new revision and digest; results from different revisions are never merged.

operations.workload: read one resource by exact typed ResourceId
read bounded simulator memory metadata by exact symbolic identity or bounded unsigned address range
read bounded TM or TC catalog metadata by exact ItemId or exact qualified name

query_rules: Identifiers are bounded ASCII tokens or exact qualified names under the selected catalog schema.
Address arithmetic uses checked unsigned integers and rejects overflow, wrap, negative length, and cross-region reads.
Every collection query has an explicit maximum result count and deterministic ItemId ordering.
No wildcard, regular expression, SQL fragment, expression, callback, or executable predicate is accepted.
Unknown identity returns typed NOT_FOUND; a disabled capability returns UNSUPPORTED; neither outcome mutates state.
A response that exceeds byte, depth, or result bounds fails closed without returning a partial success.
consistency_rules: One response is read entirely from one catalog revision and digest.
Restart reloads and verifies the same immutable bundled catalog before serving reads.
A digest mismatch makes the catalog unavailable and never falls back to a mutable working tree or legacy source.
Result ordering and canonical typed-value encoding are deterministic across SQLite and PostgreSQL control-plane deployments.
authorization_rules: The backend checks catalog and item visibility before reading or returning metadata.
Rejected reads disclose neither hidden result counts nor neighboring identifiers.
Secrets, credentials, host paths, and unapproved raw memory content are never catalog values.
forbidden_effects: generic shell, file, process, or network access
